details.label: Discussion
details.text: A loosely organized cluster of thunderstorms is tracking northwestward across parts of south-central AZ -- southeast of the Phoenix metro. Meanwhile, an outflow boundary is moving southward toward this cluster. The ongoing cluster of storms and potential outflow collision will promote a locally favorable corridor for severe wind gusts -- given temperatures in the 100-105F range and very steep low-level lapse rates

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...65-80 MPH

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: The risk of large hail and severe wind gusts should generally remain confined to parts of northwestern South Dakota in Severe Thunderstorm Watch 618

details.label: Summary
details.text: The risk of large hail and severe wind gusts should generally remain confined to parts of northwestern South Dakota in Severe Thunderstorm Watch 618

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A discrete right-moving supercell (and upstream cell development) is tracking southward across far northwestern SD, with recent reports of large hail and a severe wind gust. In the near term, this activity will continue moving southward through a corridor of weak-moderate surface-based buoyancy and around 40 kt of effective shear. This environment will continue to support discrete supercells with a risk of large to very large hail and severe wind gusts. Eventually, these storms will move into an area of increasing low-level inhibition (sampled by the UNR 00Z sounding), which should limit the severe risk with southward extent
